ci_support_linux_64_.yaml:
DOCKER_PLATFORM:
- linux/amd64
channel_sources:
- conda-forge
channel_targets:
- conda-forge main
docker_image:
- quay.io/condaforge/linux-anvil-x86_64:alma10
python_min:
- '3.11'

about.description:
phonometry (formerly published as PyOctaveBand) implements acoustic
measurement, analysis and prediction from the text of each governing
standard, and checks its results in CI against
that standard's own tables and worked examples and against further
published reference values. It covers sound level metrology (fractional
octave filter banks, frequency and time weighting, levels, dose,
calibration), psychoacoustics and hearing, speech intelligibility, room
and building acoustics, materials, vibration and structure-borne sound,
environmental, aircraft and underwater noise, electroacoustics and
broadcast loudness, and wave simulation.
about.summary: Acoustic measurement, analysis and prediction for Python, each method implemented from its standard.

script: python -c "import phonometry; assert phonometry.__version__ == '${{ version }}', phonometry.__version__"

python -c "import numpy as np, phonometry as pm; from phonometry import filters; r = filters.octave_filter(pm.Signal(np.random.default_rng(0).standard_normal(48000), 48000), fraction=3); assert len(r.frequencies) == 33"

tests.script: python -c "import numpy as np, phonometry as pm; from phonometry import filters; r = filters.octave_filter(pm.Signal(np.random.default_rng(0).standard_normal(48000), 48000), fraction=3); assert len(r.frequencies) == 33"

python -c "import matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg'); import numpy as np, phonometry as pm; from phonometry import filters; filters.octave_filter(pm.Signal(np.random.default_rng(0).standard_normal(48000), 48000), fraction=3).plot()"

name: phonometry
raw_meta_yaml:
schema_version: 1

context:
  version: "4.0.1"
  python_min: "3.12"

package:
  name: phonometry
  version: ${{ version }}

source:
  url: https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/source/p/phonometry/phonometry-${{ version }}.tar.gz
  sha256: 1318cf243efb2f49e3751bb8224e7aeca587ea296c1eff7041880da1d42c7ea8

build:
  noarch: python
  number: 0
  script: ${{ PYTHON }} -m pip install . -vv

requirements:
  host:
    - python ${{ python_min }}.*
    - pip
    - setuptools >=84.0.0
  run:
    - python >=${{ python_min }}
    # pyproject.toml raises these floors on Python 3.13 and 3.14 behind
    # python_version markers, only because older releases have no wheel
    # there. conda-forge's first builds for 3.13 (numpy 2.1.0, scipy 1.14.1)
    # and 3.14 (numpy 2.3.2, scipy 1.16.1) are the same releases, so the
    # solver keeps each Python's floor without the markers.
    - numpy >=2.0.2
    - scipy >=1.14.0
  run_constraints:
    - matplotlib-base >=3.10.7
    - numba >=0.60.0
    - pysoundfile >=0.12.0
    - reportlab >=4.3.0
    - svglib >=0.9.1,!=1.4.0
    - pytorch >=2.3.0
    - array-api-compat >=1.5.1

tests:
  - python:
      imports:
        - phonometry
        - phonometry.aircraft
        - phonometry.broadcast
        - phonometry.building
        - phonometry.electroacoustics
        - phonometry.emission
        - phonometry.environment
        - phonometry.filters
        - phonometry.fluids
        - phonometry.hearing
        - phonometry.io
        - phonometry.materials
        - phonometry.metrology
        - phonometry.noise_control
        - phonometry.psychoacoustics
        - phonometry.room
        - phonometry.signals
        - phonometry.simulation
        - phonometry.solids
        - phonometry.speech
        - phonometry.underwater
        - phonometry.vibration
      python_version:
        - ${{ python_min }}.*
        - "*"
      pip_check: true
  - package_contents:
      site_packages:
        - phonometry
      files:
        exists:
          - site-packages/phonometry/py.typed
          - site-packages/phonometry/aircraft/data/anp/*.csv
          - site-packages/phonometry/aircraft/data/anp/*.md
          - site-packages/phonometry/building/data/*.json
          - site-packages/phonometry/environment/propagation/data/*.json
          - site-packages/phonometry/fluids/data/*.json
          - site-packages/phonometry/materials/absorbers/data/*.json
          - site-packages/phonometry/materials/diffusers/data/*.json
          - site-packages/phonometry/materials/resilient/data/*.json
          - site-packages/phonometry/noise_control/data/*.json
          - site-packages/phonometry/solids/data/*.json
  - script:
      - python -c "import phonometry; assert phonometry.__version__ == '${{ version }}', phonometry.__version__"
      - python -c "from phonometry import aircraft; assert len(aircraft.load_anp_database().aircraft_ids) > 0"
      - python -c "import numpy as np, phonometry as pm; from phonometry import filters; r = filters.octave_filter(pm.Signal(np.random.default_rng(0).standard_normal(48000), 48000), fraction=3); assert len(r.frequencies) == 33"
    requirements:
      run:
        - python ${{ python_min }}.*
  - script:
      - python -c "import numpy as np, phonometry as pm; from phonometry import filters; r = filters.octave_filter(pm.Signal(np.random.default_rng(0).standard_normal(48000), 48000), fraction=3); assert len(r.frequencies) == 33"
  - script:
      - python -c "import matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg'); import numpy as np, phonometry as pm; from phonometry import filters; filters.octave_filter(pm.Signal(np.random.default_rng(0).standard_normal(48000), 48000), fraction=3).plot()"
    requirements:
      run:
        - python ${{ python_min }}.*
        - matplotlib-base >=3.10.7

about:
  homepage: https://phonometry.dev/
  repository: https://github.com/jmrplens/phonometry
  documentation: https://phonometry.dev/
  license: MIT AND LicenseRef-EASA-ANP
  license_file:
    - LICENSE
    - LICENSES/LicenseRef-EASA-ANP.txt
  summary: Acoustic measurement, analysis and prediction for Python, each method implemented from its standard.
  description: |
    phonometry (formerly published as PyOctaveBand) implements acoustic
    measurement, analysis and prediction from the text of each governing
    standard, and checks its results in CI against
    that standard's own tables and worked examples and against further
    published reference values. It covers sound level metrology (fractional
    octave filter banks, frequency and time weighting, levels, dose,
    calibration), psychoacoustics and hearing, speech intelligibility, room
    and building acoustics, materials, vibration and structure-borne sound,
    environmental, aircraft and underwater noise, electroacoustics and
    broadcast loudness, and wave simulation.

extra:
  recipe-maintainers:
    - jmrplens
